<description>
The options for wallet funding RPCs have several issues:

* snake_case aliases are accepted by the server, but unsupported by bitcoin-cli, not mentioned in the docs and rejected by the schema.
* If both the snake_case and camelCase are provided, the camelCase is silently ignored.
* The server silently ignores `subtract_fee_from_outputs`. (reported by stutxo in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35317)

Fix all issues, by:

* Adding the snake_case aliases to the CLI, docs and the schema.
* Rejecting if both are supplied.
* Reading `subtract_fee_from_outputs` instead of silently ignoring it.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6394537752 comment by fametrano (contributor):
The schema now rejects `changeAddress`, `changePosition`, `lockUnspents` and `subtractFeeFromOutputs`, which the server still accepts.

In `getopenrpcinfo` at faeb073ca68348bc663c80b3f2b70d7014466b07, the `options` object of `fundrawtransaction` and `walletcreatefundedpsbt` lists only the snake_case names, with `additionalProperties: false`. Nested properties carry no `x-bitcoin-aliases`. So the mismatch the description calls an issue is turned around, not removed: a client that validates against the schema refuses a camelCase request the server funds, and v32.0 shipped the camelCase names in this schema. Either the nested schema lists the aliases, or the camelCase names get a real deprecation, as #36488 does for `confTarget`. Today only the new error string calls them deprecated; the help and the release note do not.

Two camelCase names remain in text a user reads. The `change_type` help still says "Only valid if changeAddress is not specified", and an out-of-range position still fails with "changePosition out of bounds".

The rest matched. Without the change, `subtract_fee_from_outputs` was ignored and one spelling silently won when both were set. With it, all four options work in either spelling, in the options object, as named arguments and through `bitcoin-cli -named`, and setting both is rejected. I measured this on regtest against builds with and without this change, with calls sent through a client library I maintain. I can share the script and its output.
</new_statements>
